data: The study of politics is much more than the study of the state. It involves the examination and engagement with the social and political structures, concepts, ideas and values. Thus, concepts like equality, liberty, rights, justice, sovereignty, power, democracy, modernity, nationalism, identity, state, legitimacy and dissent become central to the discipline of politics. Political Theory I exposes the students to some of these concepts. However, the course on Political Theory II will engage with the remaining concepts through the ongoing debates around some of the concepts like sovereignty, power, nationalism, democracy, identity and modernity. The engagement with these debates bring to the surface how certain concepts complicate or simplify the understanding and applicability of other concepts in a polity. The engagement with these concepts manifests in political action. Political action aims at either preservation or change guided by the thought of better or worse. This is deeply embedded in finding the good or the right driven by what starts as a question and ends with knowledge. Thus, political theory is driven towards the pursuit of knowledge for the good of society, polity, people and collectives exhibited in the establishment of order and resolution of contestation or conflict. The engagements with ongoing debates enhances this pursuit of knowledge which is deeply embedded in explanatory wisdom for the truth. Thus, the course will engage with such a quest for knowledge while resolving ongoing contestations, conflicts and debates that aim at generating consent and acceptance for an ordered polity. The course will be anchored to the challenges to state and sovereignty, contestations over power and legitimacy, debate around dissent safeguarding democracy or democracy being dissent, paradox of modernity and identity and the elusiveness of nationalism. It is through a critical engagement and coherent analysis of the concepts and the ongoing debates and challenges around them that the course will enrich political theory and the discipline of politics as it will create the knowledge of the whole by putting the parts together.
